title: Waiting for wasps: consequences for the pollination dynamics of Ficus pertusa L.
screening_reason: Field data link crop receptivity/attractiveness timing, temporal variation in pollinator abundance, visitation and per-fig seed/wasp production; a strict one-sided/overlap effect may be reconstructable, but no common-scale coefficient plus sampling variance has yet been recovered.
notes: Anstett, Kjellberg & Bronstein 1996. Crops attracting wasps earliest were most heavily visited yet matured the fewest seeds/pollinator offspring per fig; simulation plus field data used. Highest-priority new mixed strict candidate.

title: Effects of within-tree flowering asynchrony on the dynamics of seed and wasp production in an Australian fig species
screening_reason: Within-tree crop asynchrony, seed production and wasp production are measured, but the timing exposure is plant-internal reproductive synchrony rather than explicit matching to a pollinator activity curve.
notes: Ficus rubiginosa; strong seed/wasp allocation context, not strict partner synchrony.

title: Site variation in reproductive synchrony in three neotropical figs
screening_reason: Within-tree and population reproductive synchrony and sexual-phase overlap are quantified across sites, but plant final reproductive fitness is not the paired response required by strict H1.
notes: Ficus insipida, F. petiolaris, F. pertusa; important phenology/persistence context.

title: Variation in a mutualism: phenology and the maintenance of gynodioecy in two Indian fig species
screening_reason: Male/female crop phenology, pollinator production and seed production are monitored over two years, but no explicit plant-wasp mismatch effect on final seed fitness with recoverable uncertainty is identified.
notes: Ficus exasperata and F. hispida; seasonal versus asynchronous phenology contrast.

title: Variation in reproductive success within a subtropical fig/pollinator mutualism
screening_reason: Six-year Ficus aurea-Pegoscapus study quantifies seed and wasp reproductive success among figs/crops/times, but the focal predictors are flower number/crop variation rather than a registered plant-pollinator temporal matching exposure.
notes: Ficus aurea × Pegoscapus jimenezi; strong final-fitness variability context.
